column7: finalizeAccessRequestApproval granted the role, recorded the approval, and updated the request state as three SEPARATE writes with a compensating revertGrant covering a failure in the last two. The compensation got the end STATE right, but a reported failure still left revertGrant's own "approval_race_reverted" AuditEvent row behind -- the operation's only observable effect for a request the caller was told had failed -- which FuzzStorageFaultOperations' oracle (a) flagged (REST PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/access-requests/{requestId}, CreateAccessRequestApproval#1/error). It also left a real TOCTOU window in which the role was genuinely granted before being revoked. Fixed in #2415: grant + approval record + request-state update run inside ONE storage.WithTransaction, so a reported failure means precisely "nothing happened". Proving test asserts the EFFECT (zero new audit rows after a reported failure), not a return value; verified non-vacuous by replacing internal/core/invitations.go with its 7d9d31d6^ content, against which it goes red ("expected: 0, actual: 3"). NOT guarded by a committed fuzz seed, deliberately: replaying the issue's own input against that same pre-fix file PASSES, because onlyOutcomeLogTables accepts an AuditEvent-only diff by design and short-circuits before the oracle reports -- a seed named for #2407 would certify the unfixed code as correct. See the removed knownOpenTolerances entry's replacement comment in server/faultops/fuzz_storage_fault_operations_test.go for the full measurement.
